title: NY State Assembly · District 66
area: Manhattan's West Village, SoHo, TriBeCa, Greenwich Village and part of the Lower East Side.

context.text: Open seat: longtime incumbent Deborah Glick, who has held the seat since 1991, is not seeking re-election. David Siffert won a six-way June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 27.4% of the vote, narrowly defeating Jeannine Kiely (27.3%), Ryder Kessler (22.7%), Benjamin Yee (14.0%), Corinne Arnold (4.5%) and Furhan Ahmad (3.8%). No Republican candidate qualified for the general-election ballot; Kessler, who had also won the Working Families Party primary, withdrew from that line. Siffert is running uncontested in the November 3, 2026 general election.

candidates.name: David Siffert
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary; running unopposed in the general election.

summary.text: David Siffert is a civil rights attorney and NYU Law adjunct professor who was legal director of the Surveillance Technology Oversight Project before running for office. Born and raised in Manhattan, Siffert says they have drafted more than 100 bills for the state legislature through that work and their teaching. Siffert is the Democratic nominee for this open seat and is running on housing affordability, AI regulation, and protecting immigrants and civil rights.

background.text: Born and raised in Manhattan (Morningside Heights); attended Horace Mann School from kindergarten, and has lived in the district since moving there to attend law school, nearly 20 years, according to Siffert's answers to Tribeca Citizen.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Chicago (2006) and a law degree from NYU School of Law (2009).
Works as a civil rights attorney and was Legal Director of the Surveillance Technology Oversight Project, a privacy advocacy group, leaving that role to run for office.

Says that at the Surveillance Technology Oversight Project they led the group's state legislative agenda, drafting bills and building coalitions, and that they negotiated with the NYPD on New York City Council legislation expanding the department's disclosure of surveillance technology.

Is an adjunct professor of clinical law at NYU School of Law and the founding executive director of NYU Law's State Government Initiative; teaches a State Legislative Externship pairing law students with sitting legislators to draft bills. Says they have helped write more than 100 bills.
Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary for the seat long held by Deborah Glick, who is not seeking re-election, with 27.4% of the vote in a six-candidate field.

Describes themself as non-binary (Tribeca Citizen reports they use they/them pronouns) and says they would be the first openly non-binary person elected to government office in New York State; is raising a toddler in Assembly District 66.

priorities.text: Making housing more affordable through a state Social Housing Development Authority, expanded housing vouchers, and a tax on vacant and warehoused units rather than developer subsidies.
Protecting immigrants, including making New York a sanctuary state, banning ICE from state and municipal property, and allowing New Yorkers to sue when ICE breaks the law.
Regulating artificial intelligence, citing risks to privacy, civil rights, the environment, education and jobs; says he has already drafted relevant bills.

positions.summary: Wants New York to directly build deeply affordable and social housing rather than rely primarily on subsidizing private developers, funded partly by a tax on vacant/warehoused units; does not call generally for loosening zoning to increase market-rate supply.
positions.quote: Instead of handouts to developers, New York must invest in deeply affordable housing, create a Social Housing Development Authority, and fund expanded housing vouchers, paid for by a tax on vacant and warehoused units.

positions.summary: Supports right-to-counsel for tenants facing eviction and broader tenant protections as part of addressing the housing crisis.
positions.quote: We must provide right-to-counsel to anyone facing eviction.

positions.summary: Opposes cooperation between New York government and federal immigration enforcement; supports making New York a sanctuary state and banning ICE from state/municipal property.
positions.quote: We must make New York a sanctuary state, ban ICE from state and municipal property, and allow New Yorkers to sue when ICE breaks the law.

candidates.researchNotes: Siffert has not held elected office, so there is no official voting or bill-sponsorship record; positions are drawn from his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, the only substantive public source located. No campaign website was found independent of the Ballotpedia profile and his social-media links.
